diagnosis.root_cause: The F3 legacy webhook handler (legacyApplyWebhookEvent) treats the provider event payload as the source of truth: it writes ORDER.APPROVED directly onto merchant_orders and keys fulfillment by event id, so a late/duplicate approval event rewinds an already-verified capture back to APPROVED and can mint duplicate fulfillment effects.
diagnosis.mechanism: Capture completed normally: the CAPTURE operation row is SUCCEEDED with ProviderCaptureID CAP-SCRIPT-0001 (EV-4) and the provider confirms a COMPLETED capture of 12.34 USD under the same request id (EV-9, EV-13), which is the path that seals the order as CAPTURED_VERIFIED. The order row nevertheless reads Status=APPROVED with UpdatedAt 19:22:08.856107 (EV-2), i.e. ~11 ms AFTER the capture operation was updated at 19:22:08.845393 (EV-4) and after the provider capture confirmation (EV-9). The only code path in the supplied sources that writes StatusApproved from an inbound event is legacyApplyWebhookEvent's ORDER.APPROVED branch, which unconditionally UPDATEs merchant_orders.status; the canonical applyWebhookEvent never advances or rewinds payment state from an event. The result is a financially inconsistent record: money is captured provider-side (EV-1 claimed_capture_id CAP-SCRIPT-0001, EV-9, EV-13) while the local order is presented as merely APPROVED, and the same handler's event-id-keyed effect_key allows more than one fulfillment effect for one capture.
diagnosis.proposed_fix: Stop wiring the legacy handler: have HandleWebhook dispatch to the canonical applyWebhookEvent (remove the F3 legacy selection in fixture_wiring.go). The canonical handler must remain the only event path: record a durable receipt keyed by provider event id, never write order status from an event, fulfill only when the local order is already CAPTURED_VERIFIED and the event's capture id equals the sealed provider_capture_id, and use a stable per-order effect key (e.g. 'FULFILL') so redelivered or distinct events for the same capture yield exactly one fulfillment effect.
confidence_reasons: EV-4 shows the CAPTURE operation SUCCEEDED with ProviderCaptureID CAP-SCRIPT-0001, and EV-9/EV-13 show the provider applied and confirmed a COMPLETED capture of 1234 USD under the same provider_request_id, so the capture was financially effective and should have sealed the order as verified.

EV-2 shows the order still at Status=APPROVED with UpdatedAt 19:22:08.856107, which is later than the capture operation's UpdatedAt 19:22:08.845393 (EV-4) and the provider capture confirmation (EV-9); a post-capture write therefore moved the order back to APPROVED rather than the capture never having been recorded.
EV-1 independently records the same inconsistency (order_status APPROVED alongside claimed_capture_id/provider_capture_id CAP-SCRIPT-0001), matching the journal rather than contradicting it.

Among the supplied sources, only legacyApplyWebhookEvent writes StatusApproved from an inbound event and keys fulfillment by event id, which is exactly the F3 wiring described in the file comments; the canonical handler explicitly forbids state transitions from events.
uncertainties: No merchant_webhook_events or merchant_fulfillment_effects rows are included in the evidence, so the specific ORDER.APPROVED delivery (and any duplicate fulfillment effect) is inferred from timestamp ordering and the F3 wiring, not directly observed.
fixture_wiring.go, which selects the legacy handler, is referenced in the sources but was not provided for inspection, so the exact wiring line is unconfirmed.
Evidence tier is F (scripted fixture), so this diagnosis describes the fixture's seeded defect and does not establish behavior of a real PayPal Sandbox or production integration.
The evidence cannot establish whether any downstream consumer already acted on the rewound APPROVED status or on a duplicated fulfillment effect.

patch.summary: The F3 legacy webhook handler (legacyApplyWebhookEvent) trusted the event payload as the source of truth: it rewound merchant_orders.status to APPROVED on any ORDER.APPROVED event (even after a verified capture) and keyed fulfillment by event id, allowing duplicate effects. This patch makes the legacy handler apply the canonical event semantics: it no longer writes order status from an event, it fulfills only when the local order is already CAPTURED_VERIFIED and the event's capture id matches the sealed provider_capture_id, and it uses the stable per-order effect key 'FULFILL' so redelivered or distinct events for one capture yield exactly one fulfillment effect. The F3 wiring is left intact; the defective behavior it exposes is fixed.

edits.new_text: orderID, status, err := s.webhookOrder(ctx, tx, ev.ProviderOrderID)
edits.rationale: The legacy handler discarded the local order status, so it could not gate fulfillment on CAPTURED_VERIFIED. Capture the status returned by webhookOrder so the handler can verify the order is already sealed before fulfilling.

Removes the ORDER.APPROVED branch that unconditionally rewound a verified capture back to APPROVED, and gates fulfillment on the local order already being CAPTURED_VERIFIED with an event capture id matching the sealed provider_capture_id. Events can no longer mutate payment state.

Replaces the event-id-keyed effect key with the stable per-order key 'FULFILL', so redelivered or distinct events describing the same capture produce exactly one fulfillment effect via the (order_id, effect_key) conflict guard.
